title: Nothing like Him
hookLine: there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing (42:11)
last: SIGNS OUT THERE, SIGNS IN HERE.

lines: NAME ONE THING WITH NO LIKENESS.
cards: Count the pairs in the room you're in. Two shoes. Two hands.
Socks, earrings, chairs around a table. Outside: male and female birds, day and night, hot and cold. Most things you can name have a match somewhere, a twin, a counterpart, something they're like.
Now try to name one thing that has no likeness anywhere. It's harder than it sounds. Surah Ash-Shura, verse eleven, sets up that exercise, then gives its answer.

teach.b: Verse eleven begins with creation. The Originator of the heavens and the earth. He made for you mates from among yourselves, and for the cattle, mates.
Pairs, everywhere, multiplying. Then, against all those pairs, the line. Pickthall: "Naught is as His likeness; and He is the Hearer, the Seer."
Laysa ka-mithlihi shay'. This path met this verse on day two hundred forty-eight, for its last two names. Today, the first half.
Ka means like. Mithl also means like.
Both are there: literally, there is nothing like His like. Grammarians have discussed why. Some say the doubling is emphasis: nothing, nothing at all, is like Him.
Others read it as: there isn't even anything like something like Him. Either way, the sentence closes every door to comparison twice. Surah al-Ikhlas says it in one short line.
Pickthall: "And there is none comparable unto Him." So everything in the world has a pair, and the One who made the pairs has none.
Muslims make no pictures of God, and mosques are adorned with calligraphy and pattern instead.
Muslim theologians have discussed at length how to speak about Allah at all; different schools drew the lines in different places, with this verse in view. Then the verse does something gentle.
Right after saying nothing is like Him, it says He hears and He sees.
Beyond every picture, and still listening.

how: Muslims do not make images of God; mosques are decorated with calligraphy and geometric pattern, and 42:11 and Surah al-Ikhlas are central to how Muslim theology speaks about Allah.

o: a picture or image that helps us imagine Him
like His likeness: nothing compares to Him
His names, the many ways to call on Him

games.q: nothing like Him — tap the pairs.

s: 42:11 uses two words for like in one phrase
ka and mithl: nothing is like His like, closing comparison twice.
the verse says Allah is too far away to hear
right after nothing is like Him, it says He is the Hearer, the Seer.
all Muslim schools drew the lines about Allah's attributes in the same place
they differed on how to read the attributes, with this verse in view.

games.q: the verse has just described creation in pairs: mates for people, mates for cattle. what comes next?
o: and Allah too has a pair.
pairs are the secret of the world.
games.why: nothing is like Him, and He is the Hearer, the Seer: everything has a pair, and its Maker has none.

practice: Close your eyes and notice how the mind reaches for an image whenever it thinks of anything: a face, a light, a shape.
Let each image come, and gently set it down, not that, not that, without filling the space with something better. If you pray, you might rest in the verse: nothing is like Him, and He hears.

wordCard.voice: Ka-mithlihi, like His likeness, said twice in Ash-Shura's verse to close every door to comparing Allah with anything made in pairs. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: there is nothing like His likeness, with like said twice (ka, mithl).

carryVoice: Your line: beyond every picture, still listening. Ghafir, the hidden believer, ud'uni, idfa', standing firm, the signs, and now the One with no likeness: that's the week.
